---
title: "What is the chance of at least k successes in n trials?"
---

## Question

What is the chance of at least k successes in n trials?

## Work through it

Check the binomial assumptions; identify k as an inclusive lower boundary; compute P(X >= k) as 1 - P(X <= k-1).

## Worked example: mtcars

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("mtcars")
p <- mean(d$am==1)
result <- ru_apply("binomial_at_least", n=10, k=5, prob=p)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(result, pbinom(4,10,p,lower.tail=FALSE))))
```

The output models the probability of five or more successes among ten independent hypothetical draws with fixed success probability. The model is illustrative, not an inference about all vehicles.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("binomial_at_least", n=your_n, k=your_k, prob=your_p)
```

If the question asks 'more than k', use the upper tail starting at k+1 rather than k.

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("binomial_at_least")` before treating a calculation as an inference.
